Context/Background:
Sonic hedgehog medulloblastoma (SHH-MB), characterized by hyperactivation of the namesake Sonic hedgehog (SHH) signaling pathway, accounts for ∼30% of all medulloblastoma (MB) and occurs across all age groups. Cerebellar granule neuron progenitors (GNPs) are the developmental origin of SHH-MB. Germline loss-of-function (LOF) variants in Elongator acetyltransferase complex subunit 1 (ELP1) are the most prevalent predisposing genetic events in childhood MB, accounting for ∼30% of the SHH 3 subtype. The mechanism(s) by which germline ELP1 deficiency provokes SHH-MB pathogenesis remain unknown. To resolve the mechanistic basis of ELP1-associated SHH-MB, we generated a germline Elp1+/− mouse model using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing (designated as Elp1HET mice).

We analyzed multi-omic signatures in GNPs collected from P7 Elp1HET mice compared to littermate controls. ELP1 was the only differentially expressed gene by bulk RNA-seq. Given ELP1’s crucial role in stabilizing the Elongator complex (essential for efficient translation), we performed TMT-MS and polysome profiling on isolates from P7 Elp1HET and Elp1WT GNPs.
Prompt: Based on the study context, summarize most relevant pathways and leading edge genes from the GSEA results of the differential analysis between Elp1HET and Elp1WT GNPs in both TMT-MS and polysome profiling.

Introduction/Context  
Germline Elp1 haploinsufficiency (Elp1HET) in P7 cerebellar granule neuron progenitors (GNPs) predisposes to SHH-subtype medulloblastoma. Bulk RNA-seq revealed only ELP1 as differentially expressed. To probe translational regulation, TMT-MS proteomics and polysome profiling were performed on Elp1HET versus Elp1WT GNPs. GSEA of proteomic log2FC values and of polysome-associated mRNAs identified coordinated shifts in translation, organellar metabolism, and cell‐cycle modules. Sample sizes and replicates were not specified.

Analysis  
Both modalities reveal strong repression of core translational machinery in Elp1HET GNPs—downregulated ribosomal assembly, SRP-dependent cotranslational targeting, and elongation—with ribosomal proteins (e.g., RPS27A, RPL18A, UBA52) as leading‐edge genes. Proteomics uniquely shows upregulation of peroxisomal and oxidative metabolism pathways and cytoskeletal/spindle modules, whereas polysome profiling highlights enhanced aminoacyl-tRNA biosynthesis and mitotic spindle signatures. Mitochondrial organization emerges as commonly enriched, linking translational defects to organellar remodeling. This pattern suggests that Elp1 haploinsufficiency attenuates global protein synthesis while driving compensatory metabolic and cell‐cycle responses in developing GNPs.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate key ribosomal protein downregulation (RPS27A, RPL18A) by immunoblotting in Elp1HET versus WT GNPs.  
2. Test whether boosting aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase activity rescues translational defects using small‐molecule modulators.  
3. Perform ribosome run‐off assays to quantify elongation rates under Elp1 haploinsufficiency.  
4. Examine ER stress and UPR activation given SRP pathway repression and possible Hh ligand secretion defects.
